_comment: The provider store and catalog submission preflight (issue #90 / WP5.4), and the
adapter conformance drift gate EPIC B's Phase 6 (#81) lands in it.
Read submission.go first: this file is only the declarations, and the two guards
that keep declarations honest are inherited whole from the cross-provider
conformance matrix (matrix.go). Completeness: a target that omits a capability
fails, because omission is how a matrix lies. Staleness: every declaration that is
not a plain 'supported' still has its check run, and a check that PASSES against an
unsupported, not-applicable or blocked declaration fails the cell, so this file
cannot become a list of excuses for checks nobody runs.
Everything about an adapter other than its store and its cells is read from
conformance.json: its tier, its owning EPIC, its packaging metadata, its acceptance
procedure. A target registers once, with #86's matrix, and is registered with this
UGREEN is in this mechanism and out of its gate. Its column is decided by exactly
these checks, and while EPIC D's #83 has produced no .UPK it has no artifact, so
every artifact-dependent cell is recorded not-yet-applicable rather than failing.
That is derived from the packaging metadata by HasArtifact, not declared here: 'not
ready yet' is the single most useful thing for a declaration to lie about.

drift-image-reference.reason: Decided by consuming the cross-provider conformance matrix's own verdict for this column rather than by a second check, and that verdict is NOT_APPLICABLE for canonical-image-parity: container/compose.yaml BUILDS the canonical image from container/Dockerfile rather than consuming it by reference, so there is no reference to compare. See apps/common/packaging/conformance.json.

drift-architecture-support.reason: Decided by consuming the cross-provider conformance matrix's own verdict for this column rather than by a second check, and that verdict is NOT_APPLICABLE for architecture-parity: this target makes no architecture claim of its own; it names the canonical image, whose architectures the release manifest records. See apps/common/packaging/conformance.json.

materials-description.reason: This target has no store or catalog to submit to, so there is no listing for this asset to appear on. §73's own treatment of Dockge is the shape: a distribution target supported by Compose compatibility rather than by packaging gets a documented workflow instead of a submission bundle, and docs/submission/generic.md is it.
